title: Spreadsheet with a formula engine, cycles and relative references
prompt:
Build Tabula, a small spreadsheet web app. Write the formula engine yourself; do not use a spreadsheet, parser or math library.

Grid: columns A to J and rows 1 to 30 with sticky column letters and row numbers. Above the grid, a formula bar shows the selected cell's address in a name box (for example 'E2') and the cell's raw content, so a formula cell shows its formula there and its value in the grid. The selected cell has a green outline and its column letter and row number are highlighted.

Editing and keyboard:
- Clicking a cell selects it. Typing replaces its content and starts editing; double-click or F2 edits the existing content.
- Enter commits and moves down, Tab commits and moves right, Escape cancels the edit and restores the old content. Arrow keys move the selection when not editing. Delete or Backspace clears the selected cell.
- Ctrl+Z undoes the last cell change and Ctrl+Y redoes it (at least 50 steps); dependent cells update both ways.
- Ctrl+C then Ctrl+V pastes the copied cell into the selected cell, shifting relative references by the offset (=B2*2 pasted one row down becomes =B3*2) while $-anchored parts stay fixed ($E$6, $E6, E$6).

Formulas start with '='. Support numbers, cell references, ranges such as B2:D5, the operators + - * / ^ with the usual precedence (^ first, then * and /, then + and -), unary minus, parentheses, and the functions SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX and COUNT with one or more comma-separated arguments (function names are case-insensitive). When a cell changes, every cell that depends on it, directly or through a chain, updates immediately.

Errors replace the value: '#DIV/0!' for division by zero and for AVERAGE of no numbers, '#NAME?' for an unknown function, '#VALUE!' when arithmetic uses a text cell, '#ERROR!' for a formula that cannot be parsed, and '#CYCLE!' in every cell of a circular reference. A cell that refers to an error cell shows the same error. Empty cells count as 0 in arithmetic; the five functions ignore empty and text cells.

Numbers are right-aligned and text is left-aligned. Results show at most 4 decimal places with trailing zeros removed and no thousands separators (=10/3 shows 3.3333, =1/4 shows 0.25).

Open with this Q3 sales sheet: A1 to E1 hold Region, Jul, Aug, Sep, Total; rows 2 to 5 hold North 1200 1350 980, South 860 910 1105, East 1430 1280 1390 and West 720 695 840; E2 to E5 are =SUM(B2:D2) and so on; A6 is Total and B6 to E6 sum rows 2 to 5 of their column; A7 is Average and B7 to E7 average rows 2 to 5. Row 1 and the column A labels are bold.

Save the sheet to localStorage after every change and restore it after a reload.

Visual direction: a clean productivity tool in the spirit of Google Sheets: thin gray gridlines, light gray headers, a single green accent and tabular numerals.
interaction_hints: Every scenario below starts from a fresh load (a new interact call), so B2 is 1200 unless the scenario changes it. Find cell positions from a screenshot (column headers and row numbers) or with eval on the DOM; select a cell by clicking it, then use the type action WITHOUT a selector (keyboard typing starts the edit) and press Enter. Read values from screenshots and from eval of the cell text. Enter moves down, so formulas for F2, F3, F4, F5 can be typed one after another. (1) Read the seeded values; click E2 and read the name box and formula bar; click B2, type 1500, Enter, screenshot; press Control+z, screenshot; press Control+y, screenshot. (2) F2..F5: =2+3*4^2, =(2+3)*-2, =10/3, =1/4. (3) Click G2, type =E2/$E$6*100, Enter; click G2, press Control+c; click G3, press Control+v; click G3 and read the formula bar and the value. (4) H1: =H2+1, H2: =H1*2, screenshot, then select H2, type 5, Enter. (5) Errors in I1..I5: =B2/0, =FOO(1), =A2*2, =1+, =AVERAGE(J1:J5); then I6: =I1+1. Functions in J6..J10: =MAX(B2:D5), =MIN(B2:D5), =COUNT(A1:E5), =sum(B2:B5,10), =J30+5. (6) Keyboard: select C3, type 999 and press Escape (C3 keeps 910); select C3, press Tab after typing 911 and check that D3 is selected; press ArrowLeft and Delete to clear C3 and check E3 and C6. (7) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make the changes, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot or eval again.

rubric.criterion: The grid has columns A to J and rows 1 to 30 with column letters and row numbers, and a formula bar with a name box. On load A1:E1 read Region, Jul, Aug, Sep, Total, rows 2-5 hold North/South/East/West with the given monthly numbers, A6 is Total and A7 is Average; row 1 and the column A labels are bold, numbers right-aligned and text left-aligned.
Selecting E2 shows 'E2' in the name box and =SUM(B2:D2) in the formula bar. Changing B2 to 1500 immediately shows E2 3830, B6 4510, E6 13060, B7 1127.5 and E7 3265.
Formulas follow operator precedence and number formatting: =2+3*4^2 shows 50, =(2+3)*-2 shows -10, =10/3 shows 3.3333 and =1/4 shows 0.25.
G2 with =E2/$E$6*100 shows 27.6646; copying G2 with Ctrl+C and pasting into G3 with Ctrl+V puts =E3/$E$6*100 in G3 (seen in the formula bar) and shows 22.5313.
Entering =H2+1 in H1 and =H1*2 in H2 shows #CYCLE! in both cells (no freeze, no crash); then entering 5 in H2 makes H1 show 6.
Errors: =B2/0 shows #DIV/0!, =FOO(1) shows #NAME?, =A2*2 shows #VALUE!, =1+ shows #ERROR!, =AVERAGE(J1:J5) over empty cells shows #DIV/0!, and =I1+1 where I1 holds =B2/0 also shows #DIV/0!.
Functions from a fresh load: =MAX(B2:D5) shows 1430, =MIN(B2:D5) shows 695, =COUNT(A1:E5) shows 16, =sum(B2:B5,10) shows 4220 and =J30+5 shows 5.

Keyboard editing: Enter commits and moves down, Tab commits and moves right, Escape during an edit restores the previous content, arrow keys move the selection, and Delete clears the selected cell with its dependents recalculating (clearing C3 makes E3 1965 and C6 3325).
After changing B2 to 1500, Ctrl+Z restores 1200 and E6 12760, and Ctrl+Y re-applies 1500 and E6 13060.
After editing cells (for example B2 set to 1500 and a formula typed into G2), reloading the page restores the same contents and computed values.

It looks like a polished spreadsheet: thin consistent gridlines, light gray sticky headers that stay visible when the grid scrolls, one green accent for the selection outline and the highlighted row and column headers, aligned tabular numerals, and no clipped text in the seeded table.

title: Budget dashboard with CSV import, recurring rules and monthly rollups
prompt:
Build Ledgerly, a personal budgeting dashboard for the first quarter of 2026 (January to March). The provided transactions.csv is my bank export: copy it into the output folder next to index.html and load it at runtime with fetch('transactions.csv'); never hard-code its rows. If it cannot be loaded, show an error card instead of the dashboard.

CSV rules: the first line is the header date,description,category,amount. Fields may be wrapped in double quotes, quoted fields may contain commas, and a doubled quote inside a quoted field is one literal quote character. Blank lines are ignored. A row whose date is not a real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, or whose amount is not a number, is skipped. Negative amounts are expenses and positive amounts are income. After loading, show a notice in the form 'Imported 12 transactions · 1 row skipped (line 7)', or '2 rows skipped (lines 7, 9)' for several, with the real counts and the file's line numbers (write 'transaction' for exactly one).

Starting balance on 1 January 2026: $2,500.00.

Recurring rules: a panel lists rules (description, category, amount, frequency Weekly, Every 2 weeks or Monthly, start date, optional end date) with an Add rule form and a delete button per rule. A rule generates dated transactions from its start date until its end date or 31 March 2026, whichever comes first. Monthly rules repeat on the start day and fall back to the last day of shorter months (a rule starting 31 January lands on 28 February). Generated transactions show a recurring badge in the list and count everywhere. Seed one rule: 'Streaming subscription', Entertainment, -15.99, Monthly from 2026-01-20.

Dashboard:
- Period tabs Jan, Feb, Mar and Q1 (the default).
- Four stat cards for the selected period: Income, Expenses (shown as a positive total), Net and Closing balance.
- A monthly rollup table with Month, Income, Expenses, Net and Closing balance for the three months.
- A Chart.js grouped bar chart of income vs expenses per month, and a Chart.js doughnut of expenses by category for the selected period next to a table of each category's total and its share of the period's expenses with one decimal (like 12.5%).
- A transaction list with a category filter, a text search on the description, sorting by date or amount from the column headers, and a 'Showing N of M' label.
- A 'Paste CSV' dialog with a textarea: pasted rows (same format, header optional) are appended with the same validation and their own notice, where line numbers count lines of the pasted text.

Money always shows as $1,234.56 with a leading minus for negatives (-$1,450.00). Rules and pasted rows persist in localStorage; the CSV is re-read from disk on every visit.

Visual direction: a calm fintech look with white cards on a pale gray-blue background, one teal accent, tabular numerals, green for income and red for expenses. At 390px wide everything stacks in one column and wide tables scroll inside their cards.
interaction_hints: The input file is /grader/task/transactions.csv; grep the page's HTML/JS for a relative fetch of transactions.csv (hard-coded rows fail R1). Q1 is the default tab. Date inputs accept type with a selector and a value like 2026-01-06. If clicking a select option does not work, use the select action or set it with eval (assign .value and dispatch input and change events). Suggested calls from a fresh load each: (1) screenshot, read the notice, stat cards, rollup table and category table; search the list for Luigi and for Rent. (2) Add rule Coffee beans, Groceries, -12.50, Weekly, start 2026-01-06, no end; screenshot Q1 and the Mar tab; count list rows with the recurring badge for that description (13 expected); then delete the rule and check the totals return. (3) Add rule Savings transfer, Savings, -300, Monthly, start 2026-01-31; look for its dates 2026-01-31, 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-31 and the Feb expenses. (4) Open Paste CSV and type two lines 2026-03-20,Concert tickets,Entertainment,-85.00 and 2026-13-01,Bad row,Other,-1 (newline between them), submit, read the notice and the Mar numbers. (5) Filter Groceries, then search rent, then click the Amount header. (6) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make the changes, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot or eval again. (7) Missing file: copy /grader/artifact to /tmp/nocsv, delete transactions.csv there and run interact with --artifact-dir /tmp/nocsv. Check mobile.png.

rubric.criterion: transactions.csv is in the output folder and loaded at runtime with a relative fetch; the notice reads 'Imported 36 transactions · 2 rows skipped (lines 25, 32)', the 2026-01-17 Dining row shows Luigi's wrapped in literal double-quote characters (the CSV's doubled quotes decoded), and 'Rent, January' keeps its comma.
With Q1 selected and the seeded streaming rule, the stat cards read Income $10,662.00, Expenses $6,098.56, Net $4,563.44 and Closing balance $7,063.44, and the list says 'Showing 39 of 39'.

A Chart.js grouped bar chart shows income and expenses for Jan, Feb and Mar, and a Chart.js doughnut plus a category table show Q1 expenses by category with Housing $4,350.00 at 71.3%, Groceries $523.17 at 8.6% and Health $104.99 at 1.7%.

Adding the weekly rule Coffee beans (Groceries, -12.50, from 2026-01-06) adds 13 transactions with a recurring badge, makes Mar expenses $2,113.83 and Q1 expenses $6,261.06 with a Q1 closing balance of $6,900.94; deleting the rule restores the previous numbers.
A monthly rule Savings transfer (-300 from 2026-01-31) creates transactions dated 2026-01-31, 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-31, and Feb expenses become $2,363.33.

Pasting the rows 2026-03-20,Concert tickets,Entertainment,-85.00 and 2026-13-01,Bad row,Other,-1 shows 'Imported 1 transaction · 1 row skipped (line 2)', adds only the concert, and Mar expenses become $2,136.33.
Selecting the Mar tab changes the cards to Income $3,812.00, Expenses $2,051.33, Net $1,760.67 and Closing balance $7,063.44, and the doughnut and category table switch to March (Housing 70.7%).
The Groceries filter shows 'Showing 8 of 39', searching 'rent' lists exactly the three rent rows, and clicking the Amount header sorts the list by amount (clicking again reverses it).
An added rule survives a reload, and with transactions.csv missing the page shows an error card instead of a broken or empty dashboard.
At 390px wide the cards, charts, rollup and list stack in one column; wide tables scroll inside their cards and nothing is clipped or overlapping.
A polished fintech look: white cards on a pale gray-blue background, one teal accent, green income and red expense amounts, right-aligned tabular numbers and consistent card radii and spacing.

title: Kanban with swimlanes, WIP limits, keyboard moves and undo
prompt:
Build Flowboard, a kanban board with swimlanes and WIP limits for a product team, fully usable with mouse and keyboard.

Columns, left to right: Backlog, Ready, In progress (WIP limit 3), Review (WIP limit 2), Done. Swimlanes, top to bottom: Expedite, Platform, Mobile. Each column header shows its name, 'cards/limit' for limited columns (like '1/3') or just the card count for the others, and the column's story-point total (like '8 pts'); column numbers count all lanes. Each lane header shows its name and card count and can be collapsed.

Seed exactly these cards (ID, title, lane, column, points, assignee initials):
FLW-101 Fix checkout crash on iOS 18, Expedite, In progress, 3, MK
FLW-102 Migrate auth to OAuth 2.1, Platform, In progress, 8, JS
FLW-103 Rate-limit public API, Platform, Review, 5, AL
FLW-104 Offline mode for notes, Mobile, In progress, 8, MK
FLW-105 Dark mode polish, Mobile, Review, 2, RB
FLW-106 Upgrade Postgres to 17, Platform, Ready, 5, JS
FLW-107 Push notification settings, Mobile, Ready, 3, RB
FLW-108 Audit logging, Platform, Backlog, 5, AL
FLW-109 Tablet layout, Mobile, Backlog, 8, MK
FLW-110 Release 4.2 notes, Mobile, Done, 1, RB
FLW-111 CDN cache purge tool, Platform, Done, 3, JS
FLW-112 Hotfix: expired TLS cert, Expedite, Done, 2, AL
Cards show the ID, title, a points chip and an initials avatar.

WIP rules: moving a Platform or Mobile card into a column that is already at its limit is refused: the card stays put and a toast says 'WIP limit reached: Review (2/2)' with that column's name and numbers. Expedite cards ignore limits; a column over its limit gets a red header showing the count, like '4/3'.

Moving cards:
- Drag and drop with the mouse into any lane and column cell.
- Keyboard: clicking a card focuses it with a visible focus ring. Arrow keys move the focus between cards. Shift+ArrowRight and Shift+ArrowLeft move the focused card to the next or previous column in its lane; Shift+ArrowUp and Shift+ArrowDown move it to the lane above or below. The moved card keeps focus.
- Enter opens a card editor dialog (title, points, assignee, lane); Escape closes it and returns focus to the card. Delete removes the focused card.
- The N key opens a 'New card' dialog; new cards get the next ID (FLW-113, FLW-114, ...) and land in the Backlog of the chosen lane.

Undo and redo: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z, plus toolbar buttons that are disabled when there is nothing to undo or redo, cover moves, creates, edits and deletes. A refused move creates no undo step.

Filters: a search box matching ID or title, and assignee avatar toggles in the header. A 'Showing N of M cards' label updates; column and lane numbers keep counting all cards.

Persist the board to localStorage and restore it after a reload.

Visual direction: a calm, dense tool in the spirit of Linear: light gray canvas, white cards, one violet accent, red only for WIP problems, clear lane separators.
interaction_hints: Click a card by its ID text (for example the selector text=FLW-106) to focus it, then press keys such as Shift+ArrowRight. Read column headers and the toast from screenshots or eval of the DOM text. Suggested calls from a fresh load each: (1) screenshot and read all column headers; click FLW-106, press Shift+ArrowRight, screenshot within 1 s for the toast; check the Undo button is still disabled. (2) Click FLW-103, Shift+ArrowRight (to Done); click FLW-102, Shift+ArrowRight (to Review); click FLW-106, Shift+ArrowRight (to In progress); screenshot the headers; press Control+z, screenshot; press Control+Shift+z, screenshot. Also click FLW-107 and press Shift+ArrowUp to move it to the Platform lane. (3) Press n, create 'Payment outage', 5 points, lane Expedite; focus the new card and press Shift+ArrowRight twice; screenshot the In progress header. (4) Drag FLW-109 (Mobile, Backlog) to the Mobile lane of Ready using the drag action with steps 25 or more (read coordinates from a screenshot; retry with a hover first if nothing moves). (5) Click FLW-104, press Enter, change points to 13, save, check the In progress total; press Enter again then Escape and check focus returns (eval document.activeElement.textContent). Delete: focus FLW-111, press Delete, then Control+z. (6) Toggle the MK avatar filter, then clear it and search api. (7) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make the changes, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot or eval again.

rubric.criterion: The board has columns Backlog, Ready, In progress, Review and Done in that order, lanes Expedite, Platform and Mobile, and the twelve seeded cards FLW-101 to FLW-112 in the specified lane and column cells, each with ID, title, points chip and initials avatar.
On load the column headers read: Backlog 2 cards and 13 pts, Ready 2 and 8 pts, In progress 3/3 and 19 pts, Review 2/2 and 7 pts, Done 3 and 6 pts.
With FLW-106 focused, Shift+ArrowRight is refused: FLW-106 stays in Ready and a toast reads 'WIP limit reached: In progress (3/3)'; the undo control stays disabled because no step was recorded.

Keyboard moves work: FLW-103 to Done makes Review 1/2 and Done 4 cards and 11 pts; FLW-102 to Review then FLW-106 to In progress makes In progress 3/3 and 16 pts; the moved card keeps focus, and Shift+ArrowUp on FLW-107 moves it to the Platform lane in the same column.

Undo and redo: after the moves above, Ctrl+Z puts FLW-106 back in Ready (In progress 2/3, 11 pts) and Ctrl+Shift+Z moves it back; deleting a focused card with Delete removes it and Ctrl+Z restores it in the same place.
Pressing N and creating 'Payment outage' (5 pts, Expedite) adds FLW-113 to the Expedite Backlog; moving it into the full In progress column is allowed and that header turns red and shows 4/3.
Dragging FLW-109 with the mouse from Mobile Backlog to Mobile Ready moves it there: Ready shows 3 cards and 16 pts and Backlog 1 card and 5 pts.
Enter on a focused card opens the editor; changing FLW-104 to 13 points updates the In progress total to 24 pts; Escape closes the dialog and focus returns to that card.
Filtering by the MK avatar shows only FLW-101, FLW-104 and FLW-109 with 'Showing 3 of 12 cards' while column headers still count all cards; searching 'api' shows only FLW-103.
After several moves and an edit, reloading the page restores every card in the same lane, column, order and with the same points.
Lanes and columns form an aligned grid with consistent gaps; long titles wrap inside cards; collapsing a lane hides its cards and keeps its header with the count.

It looks like a polished, dense productivity tool: light gray canvas, white cards with subtle borders or shadows, one violet accent, a clear focus ring, red used only for WIP problems, and legible hierarchy between column, lane and card text.

title: Calendar with recurring events, exceptions and conflict detection
prompt:
Build Cadence, a calendar web app with recurring events and conflict detection. Use a fixed today of Wednesday 14 October 2026 (do not read the system clock); the app opens on that week.

Views, with hash routing so a reload keeps the view: Week (#/week/2026-10-12, the default), Month (#/month/2026-10) and Agenda (#/agenda, the 14 days starting today). Weeks start on Monday. The toolbar shows the range title (like 'Nov 2 – 8, 2026' or 'November 2026'), previous and next buttons, a Today button and the view switcher. Keyboard (ignored while typing in a field): ArrowLeft and ArrowRight go to the previous and next period, T to today, W, M and A switch views, N opens the new-event dialog.

Week view: an hourly grid from 07:00 to 21:00 with 30-minute lines, one column per day, today's column tinted, events placed by start and end time. Overlapping events on the same day are drawn side by side and both get a red conflict marker; events that only touch (one ends exactly when the next starts) do not conflict. A sidebar shows 'Conflicts this week: N' and 'Busy this week: 7h 45m' style totals, where busy time is the union of all event time in the week, so overlapping time counts once. Clicking an empty slot opens the new-event dialog with that day and half hour filled in.

Month view: a 6-row grid starting on Monday, days outside the month dimmed, up to 3 event chips per day and '+N more' beyond that.

Events have a title, date, start and end time, color, and a repeat rule: none, weekly on chosen weekdays, every 2 weeks on chosen weekdays, or monthly on the same day number (months without that day are skipped, so a rule on the 31st has no November occurrence). A rule can end never, on a date, or after N occurrences. Validation errors appear under the fields: 'Title is required' and 'End time must be after start time'.

Clicking an event opens a popover with its details, Edit and Delete. For a recurring event, Edit and Delete ask 'This event' or 'All events'; 'This event' changes or removes only that occurrence.

Seed these events (all 2026):
- Team standup, 09:30–09:45, weekly Mon–Fri, from Mon 28 Sep until Fri 18 Dec
- Design review, 14:00–15:00, every 2 weeks on Wednesday, from Wed 30 Sep
- 1:1 with Priya, 11:00–11:30, weekly on Thursday, from Thu 1 Oct
- Gym, 18:00–19:00, weekly Mon, Wed and Fri, from Mon 28 Sep
- Payroll run, 10:00–11:00, monthly on the 15th, from 15 Jan
- Sprint demo, 16:00–17:00, every 2 weeks on Friday, from Fri 2 Oct
- Quarterly planning, Wed 14 Oct, 13:30–16:00, one-off
- Dentist, Fri 16 Oct, 09:00–10:00, one-off

Save all events and exceptions in localStorage.

Visual direction: clean and airy like Google Calendar: white surfaces, light gridlines, soft pastel event colors with darker text, tabular time labels and a single blue accent. At 390px wide the week view shows three days at a time with the same controls.
interaction_hints: Use screenshots plus eval of the sidebar text. Keys: ArrowRight/ArrowLeft after clicking an empty non-input area. Time and date inputs accept type with a selector (values like 07:30 and 2026-10-13). If clicking a select option does not work, use the select action or set it with eval (assign .value and dispatch input and change events). Suggested calls from a fresh load each: (1) screenshot the week, read the title, both sidebar stats and which events carry conflict markers (Thu Payroll 10:00-11:00 and 1:1 11:00-11:30 only touch). (2) Press ArrowRight, screenshot and read the stats; ArrowRight again, screenshot; press t. (3) Click the Wed 14 Oct Gym block, Delete, choose 'This event'; read Busy; check Mon and Fri Gym remain and next week's Wed Gym exists. (4) Create Yoga on 2026-10-13 07:30-08:15, weekly on Tue and Thu, ending after 4 occurrences; read Busy; check the next week (Tue 20, Thu 22) and the week after (none). (5) Click the Fri 16 Oct Team standup, Edit, This event, set 10:00-10:15, save; read conflicts, Busy, and check Thursday's standup is still 09:30. (6) Create Rent reminder on 2026-10-31 08:00-08:30 repeating monthly; open month view (m) and go to November and December. (7) Month view of October: check the first cell (Mon 28 Sep) and the '+1 more' on the 14th and 16th. (8) Validation: open the dialog, clear the title and set end before start, save. (9) Reload at #/month/2026-10 keeps month view. (10) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make the changes, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot or eval again. Check mobile.png.

rubric.criterion: The app opens on the week titled 'Oct 12 – 18, 2026' starting Monday, with a 07:00-21:00 grid with 30-minute lines, Wednesday 14 October tinted as today, and previous, next, Today and Week/Month/Agenda controls.

That week shows exactly 14 events in the right places: Team standup 09:30 Mon to Fri, Gym 18:00 Mon, Wed and Fri, Design review 14:00 and Quarterly planning 13:30-16:00 on Wed, Payroll run 10:00 and 1:1 with Priya 11:00 on Thu, Dentist 09:00 and Sprint demo 16:00 on Fri.

The sidebar reads 'Conflicts this week: 2' and busy time 10h 0m (10h 00m also passes); Quarterly planning and Design review, and Dentist and Team standup, are drawn side by side with conflict markers, while Payroll run and 1:1 with Priya are not marked.

ArrowRight (or next) shows 'Oct 19 – 25, 2026' with 9 events, 0 conflicts and busy 4h 45m, with no Design review or Sprint demo; the following week shows Design review on Wed 28 Oct and Sprint demo on Fri 30 Oct with busy 6h 45m.
Deleting only the Wed 14 Oct Gym occurrence ('This event') removes just that block: busy becomes 9h 0m, Gym remains on Mon 12 and Fri 16, and Gym still appears on Wed 21 Oct.
Creating Yoga on Tue 13 Oct 07:30-08:15, weekly on Tue and Thu, ending after 4 occurrences, shows it on Oct 13, 15, 20 and 22 only, and busy for the week of Oct 12 becomes 11h 30m.

Editing only the Fri 16 Oct Team standup to 10:00-10:15 moves just that occurrence: conflicts drop to 1 (touching the Dentist's 10:00 end is not a conflict), busy becomes 10h 15m, and the other standups stay at 09:30.
A monthly event created on Sat 31 Oct 2026 appears on 31 October and 31 December but has no November occurrence.
Month view for October 2026 starts with Monday 28 September, dims the days outside October, and shows '+1 more' on the 14th and the 16th, which each have four events.
Validation shows 'Title is required' and 'End time must be after start time' and saves nothing; reloading #/month/2026-10 reopens the month view; ArrowRight, T and M work from the keyboard.
After creating an event and deleting one occurrence, reloading the page keeps both changes.

The grid is clean and aligned (events line up with their time labels, side-by-side conflicts do not overlap text), and at 390px wide the week view shows three day columns with readable events and the controls still visible.

title: Regex tester with live highlighting, groups, worker timeout and share links
prompt:
Build Patternly, a regular-expression tester for JavaScript regex syntax.

Top: a pattern field shown between slashes with the active flags after it, and toggle buttons for the flags g, i, m, s and u (g on by default). Below it, a test-text editor whose matches are highlighted in place as you type, alternating two highlight colors so neighboring matches stay distinguishable; highlights must stay exactly aligned with the text while it wraps and scrolls. A status line reads '3 matches', '1 match' or 'No matches', followed by the evaluation time in ms.

Matches table: one row per match with the columns #, Index (start–end, end exclusive, like 4–9), Match, and one column per capture group headed by its number and, for named groups, its name (like '1 · year'). A group that did not take part in the match shows an em dash '—'. Zero-length matches are listed with an empty match, and the search must advance past them instead of looping forever. Without the g flag only the first match is found.

Replace tab: a replacement field supporting $1, $<name>, $& and $$, with a live preview of the whole output text.

Errors: an invalid pattern shows 'Invalid pattern: ' followed by the engine's error message in red under the field; highlights and the table clear, and nothing throws.

Safety: matching runs in a Web Worker. If it takes longer than 1000 ms, terminate the worker, show 'Timed out after 1000 ms', keep the page responsive, and let the next edit work normally.

Test cases panel: add strings with an expectation (Should match or Should not match); each shows PASS or FAIL against the current pattern and flags (a string matches when the regex finds a match anywhere in it), with a summary like '2/3 passing'.

Library: presets 'ISO date', 'Email', 'Hex color' and 'IPv4' that load a pattern and sample text; 'Save pattern' stores the current pattern, flags and text under a name in a 'My patterns' list (click to load, × to delete) kept in localStorage.

Share: the URL hash always encodes the pattern, flags and text, so reloading the page or opening a copied link restores the exact state; a 'Copy link' button copies it.

Default state: pattern (?<year>\d{4})-(?<month>\d{2})-(?<day>\d{2}) with flag g, replacement $<day>/$<month>/$<year>, and this three-line text:
Release 2.4 shipped on 2026-03-14.

title: Multi-document markdown editor with tables, footnotes and task lists
prompt:
Build Inkwell, a multi-document markdown editor with a live preview. Write the markdown parser yourself; do not bundle a markdown library.

Layout: a documents sidebar, the editor (a monospace textarea), the rendered preview and an Outline panel. The top bar shows the document title, word and character counts, and the reading time as 'N min read' (words divided by 200, rounded up, minimum 1).

Documents: the sidebar lists documents by last edit, newest first. 'New document' creates 'Untitled 1', 'Untitled 2' and so on; double-clicking a name renames it inline; deleting asks for confirmation in an in-page dialog (never window.confirm). The URL hash is #/doc/<id> for the open document, so a reload reopens it. Everything autosaves to localStorage.

The parser supports:
- ATX headings # to #### with id slugs: lowercase, punctuation removed, spaces turned into hyphens; a repeated slug gets -1, -2 (two '## Getting Started!' headings get the ids getting-started and getting-started-1)
- paragraphs, **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `inline code`, [links](url) that open in a new tab, and backslash escapes
- fenced code blocks with an optional language shown as a small label, content kept verbatim and HTML-escaped
- blockquotes, horizontal rules, and ordered and unordered lists nested by two-space indentation
- task list items '- [ ]' and '- [x]' rendered as checkboxes; clicking a checkbox in the preview toggles the matching [ ] or [x] in the editor text
- GFM tables: a header row, a delimiter row that sets each column's alignment (:--- left, :---: center, ---: right), inline formatting inside cells and \| for a literal pipe
- footnotes: [^label] references become superscript links numbered 1, 2, 3 in order of first reference; a 'Footnotes' section at the end lists the definitions in that order, each with a ↩ link back to its reference; a reference without a definition stays literal text
Raw HTML typed in the editor is shown as text, never rendered.

Outline: the H1 to H3 headings as a nested list that updates live; clicking an entry scrolls the preview to that heading.

Export: an 'Export HTML' button opens a dialog showing a complete standalone HTML document for the current text (doctype, a title element with the document name, the rendered body) with a 'Download .html' button.

On first run, create one document 'Welcome to Inkwell' that demonstrates every feature, including a table, a task list and two footnotes.

Visual direction: a calm writing tool with warm off-white paper, a serif body in the preview (DejaVu Serif or Liberation Serif), a slim sidebar and a single ink-blue accent.
interaction_hints: Replace the editor text with the type action and the textarea selector (page.fill keeps newlines and fires input). Test document, one line per item, joined with \n in the JSON text: '# Trip Plan' / '' / '## Getting Started!' / '' / '| Item | Qty | Price |' / '|:-----|:---:|------:|' / '| **Tent** | 1 | $120 |' / '| Stove \| fuel | 2 | $45 |' (the editor must receive ONE backslash before that pipe, so write two inside the JSON string) / '' / '- [ ] Book campsite' / '- [x] Buy maps' / ' - Topo map' (two leading spaces) / ' - Trail map' / '' / 'Pack light[^w] and check the forecast[^1]. See [^missing].' / '' / '## Getting Started!' / '' / 'raw' / '' / '[^1]: Mountain forecast.' / '[^w]: Under 12 kg.'. Then inspect the preview with eval: heading ids, table th/td text-align (getComputedStyle), strong inside the first cell, the checkboxes, nested ul, the footnote superscripts and the Footnotes list order, and that raw is literal text. Click the first checkbox in the preview and read the textarea value. Reading time: eval to set the textarea to 450 words ('word '.repeat(450)) and dispatch an input event, then read the top bar. Documents: click New document, rename it by double-click, check location.hash, switch documents. Delete: Playwright auto-dismisses window.confirm, so a native confirm fails the delete. Outline: click the second 'Getting Started!' entry and check the preview scrolled (scrollTop or screenshot). Export: open Export HTML and read the dialog text. localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make the changes, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot or eval again.

rubric.criterion: The app shows a documents sidebar, the monospace editor, the preview and an Outline panel, with words, characters and 'N min read' in the top bar; the first-run document 'Welcome to Inkwell' renders a table, a task list and two footnotes.
The test table renders as a table with 3 columns and 2 body rows; the columns are left, center and right aligned; 'Tent' is bold inside its cell and the second row's first cell reads 'Stove | fuel'.

Footnotes are numbered by first reference: [^w] becomes superscript 1 and [^1] becomes 2; the Footnotes section lists 'Under 12 kg.' then 'Mountain forecast.' with working ↩ back-links, and '[^missing]' stays literal text.

Task items render as checkboxes (the second checked) with a nested list of Topo map and Trail map under Buy maps; clicking the first checkbox in the preview changes the editor line to '- [x] Book campsite'.
Headings get the ids trip-plan, getting-started and getting-started-1, and the literal text raw appears in the preview instead of bold text.
The Outline lists Trip Plan with the two 'Getting Started!' entries nested under it, updates as the text changes, and clicking an entry scrolls the preview to that heading.
With 450 words in the editor the top bar shows 450 words and '3 min read'; counts update live while typing.
New document creates 'Untitled 1' and opens it (hash #/doc/<id>), double-click rename works, and switching between documents shows each one's own text.
Deleting a document asks for confirmation in an in-page dialog (no native confirm) and removes it from the sidebar only after confirming.
After editing and reloading, the same document reopens from the hash with its edited text, and the other documents are still listed.

Export HTML shows a complete document starting with a <!DOCTYPE html> doctype (any letter case) whose title element holds the document name and whose body contains the rendered HTML (headings with ids, the table, footnotes).

A calm, polished writing tool: warm off-white paper, a serif preview body with a clear heading scale and comfortable line length, well-styled tables, code blocks, task lists and footnotes, and one ink-blue accent.

title: Weighted graph editor with Dijkstra, step mode and minimum spanning tree
prompt:
Build Pathfinder, a weighted-graph editor that visualizes shortest paths and spanning trees, drawn with SVG.

Canvas: a large SVG area with a subtle dot grid. Nodes are circles with a letter label; edges are lines with the weight in a small pill at their midpoint. Seed this graph (node positions are up to you, but keep it readable with no overlapping labels):
Nodes A to H.
Edges, written from–to weight: A–B 7, A–C 3, C–B 2, B–D 6, C–E 9, E–D 4, D–F 8, F–E 5, F–G 1, D–G 13, F–H 10, E–H 16, H–G 12.

Tools (toolbar buttons with SVG icons, plus keyboard shortcuts): Move (V), Add node (N) and Add edge (E).
- Move: drag nodes and their edges follow. Click a node or an edge to select it; Delete removes the selection (deleting a node removes its edges).
- Add node: clicking empty canvas adds a node named with the next unused letter (I, J, ...).
- Add edge: click a first and a second node, type a weight in a small inline field and press Enter. Weights are whole numbers from 1 to 99; anything else shows 'Weight must be a whole number from 1 to 99'. A second edge between the same two nodes shows 'Edge already exists'.
- Double-clicking a weight pill edits it with the same validation.

Directed mode: a 'Directed' switch turns every edge into an arrow from its first node to its second (as written above, so F–E points from F to E), and every algorithm respects direction.

Algorithms panel:
- Start and End selects and 'Find path' run Dijkstra: the path's nodes and edges are highlighted and the route and total are shown like 'A → C → B · 5'. When the end cannot be reached, show 'No path from A to I' (with the actual names).
- A distance table for every node (Node, Distance, Via) with ∞ and — for unreachable nodes, and the order in which Dijkstra finalized the nodes, shown as 'Visit order: A, ...'.
- 'Step' replays the same run one finalized node at a time (finalized nodes shaded, the current node ringed, the table filling in); 'Reset' clears it.
- 'Minimum spanning tree' (undirected mode only; disabled with a short note in directed mode) highlights the tree edges found with Kruskal's algorithm and shows 'MST weight: N · K edges'; when the graph is disconnected it shows the spanning forest's weight and 'Graph is disconnected'.

History and data: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo every graph change (nodes, edges, weights, moves, deletions). An Export / Import panel shows the graph as JSON with nodes (id, x, y), edges (from, to, weight) and the directed flag, and applies edited JSON, with an error message for invalid input. The graph persists in localStorage.

Visual direction: a crisp technical tool: white canvas with a faint dot grid, slate nodes, amber for paths, teal for the spanning tree, and a compact side panel with tabular numbers.
interaction_hints: Read node and pill positions from a screenshot or with eval on the SVG (circle cx/cy plus the svg's getBoundingClientRect). If clicking a select option does not work, use the select action or set it with eval (assign .value and dispatch input and change events). Suggested calls from a fresh load each: (1) select Start A and End H, Find path, screenshot, read the result line, distance table and visit order. (2) Toggle Directed, Find path A to H, then A to G; check the MST button is disabled. (3) Undirected: click Minimum spanning tree, screenshot, read the weight and which edges are highlighted. (4) Click Step three times, screenshot after each. (5) Double-click the C–B pill, type 9, Enter; Find path A to B and A to H; run MST. (6) Press n (Add node), click empty canvas: node I appears; Find path A to I; MST; then Add edge H then I with weight 3; Find path A to I. (7) Validation: Add edge between two unconnected nodes with 0, then 100, then abc; Add edge A then B. (8) Move tool: select node F, press Delete, Find path A to H and A to G; press Control+z and check F and its 4 edges are back. (9) Drag node A somewhere else and check its edges follow. (10) Export/Import: read the JSON, change a weight in it, apply; then apply invalid JSON. (11) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make the changes, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot or eval again.

rubric.criterion: The canvas shows nodes A to H and the 13 seeded edges with the given weights in pills, readable without overlapping labels; the toolbar has Move, Add node and Add edge with SVG icons, and the side panel has Start/End, Find path, Step, Reset, Minimum spanning tree, Directed and Export/Import.

Undirected A to H shows 'A → C → E → F → H · 27' with those nodes and edges highlighted; the table reads A 0, B 5 via C, C 3 via A, D 11 via B, E 12 via C, F 17 via E, G 18 via F, H 27 via F, and the visit order is A, C, B, D, E, F, G, H.
In directed mode edges are arrows (F→E points from F to E); A to H gives 'A → C → E → H · 28' and A to G gives 'A → C → B → D → F → G · 20'; the MST button is disabled with a note.
Minimum spanning tree shows 'MST weight: 31 · 7 edges' and highlights exactly F–G, C–B, A–C, E–D, F–E, B–D and F–H.
Step replays the run one node at a time in the order A, C, B, ..., with finalized nodes shaded, the current node ringed and the table filling in; Reset clears the highlight.
After double-clicking the C–B pill and setting it to 9, A to B becomes 'A → B · 7', A to H is still 27 via A → C → E → F → H, and the MST weight becomes 36.

Adding a node creates I; A to I shows 'No path from A to I' with ∞ for I in the table and MST reports 'Graph is disconnected'; after adding edge H–I with weight 3, A to I is 'A → C → E → F → H → I · 30'.
Weights 0, 100 and abc are rejected with 'Weight must be a whole number from 1 to 99', and a second A–B edge shows 'Edge already exists'.
Deleting node F removes it with its edges: A to H becomes 'A → C → E → H · 28' and A to G 'A → C → B → D → G · 24'; Ctrl+Z restores F and its four edges.
Dragging a node in Move mode moves it with its edges and pill labels following, and after changes and a reload the graph (including positions) is restored.
Export shows the graph JSON with 8 nodes and 13 edges; editing a weight in the JSON and applying updates the canvas, and invalid JSON shows an error without changing the graph.

A crisp technical look: faint dot grid, consistent node and pill styling, amber path and teal MST highlights that stand out, arrowheads that end at node borders, and a compact aligned side panel with tabular numbers.

title: Vector drawing app with layers, inspector, alignment and history
prompt:
Build Vectra, a vector drawing app with layers, built on SVG (no canvas or drawing library).

Layout: a top bar (app name, Undo, Redo, 'Export SVG'), a left tool rail, an 800×500 white artboard centered on a gray workspace, and a right panel with the Inspector above the Layers panel. A status bar shows the pointer position in artboard coordinates (like 'x 120 · y 48', origin at the artboard's top-left corner, whole pixels) and the active tool.

Tools, as rail buttons with SVG icons and shortcuts: Select (V), Rectangle (R), Ellipse (E), Line (L), Text (T).
- Drag on the artboard to draw; holding Shift makes rectangles square, ellipses circular and lines snap to 45° steps. A click without dragging draws nothing. New rectangles and ellipses are filled #6366F1 with no stroke; lines are 2 px #111827. Text: click to place, type, then Enter or Escape to finish; default 24 px Inter in #111827.
- After drawing, the tool switches back to Select and the new shape is selected.

Selection (Select tool): a click selects the topmost shape under the pointer; Shift+click adds or removes shapes; dragging on empty artboard draws a marquee that selects every shape entirely inside it. Selected shapes show a bounding box with 8 resize handles, and dragging a handle resizes. Dragging a selected shape moves it; arrow keys nudge by 1 px and Shift+arrow by 10 px. Delete removes the selection, Ctrl+D duplicates it 10 px right and 10 px down, Escape deselects.

Inspector for one selected shape: X, Y, W and H (whole pixels, the shape's bounding box in artboard coordinates), Fill, Stroke, Stroke width and Opacity (0–100%). Typing a value and pressing Enter updates the shape at once, and dragging or nudging updates the fields. With two or more shapes selected it shows Align left, center, right, top, middle and bottom, which align to the selection's bounding box.

Layers: the document starts with 'Layer 1'. The + button adds 'Layer 2', 'Layer 3' and so on above the others and makes the new layer active; new shapes go into the active layer. Each layer row has a visibility eye (hidden layers are not drawn and their shapes cannot be selected), a lock (locked shapes cannot be selected or changed), up and down buttons that change the stacking order, and double-click to rename. Each layer lists its shapes, named per type across the document ('Rectangle 1', 'Rectangle 2', 'Ellipse 1', ...); clicking a shape row selects it.

History: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo every change (draw, move, resize, style, delete, duplicate and layer changes), at least 50 steps.

Export SVG opens a dialog with the SVG markup: viewBox '0 0 800 500' and one g element per visible layer in stacking order (bottom first) carrying the layer name in a data-name attribute.

The document autosaves to localStorage and is restored after a reload.

Visual direction: a professional design tool in the spirit of Figma: dark charcoal chrome around a gray workspace, crisp 1.5 px line icons, a blue selection color, compact 12–13 px UI labels and tabular numbers in the inspector.
interaction_hints: First find the artboard's screen origin: eval the bounding rect of the artboard element (or hover and read the status bar coordinates). Page point = origin + artboard point. Use drag with steps 20 or more; for Shift-constrained drawing use keydown Shift, drag, keyup Shift. Inspector fields: type with a selector then press Enter. Suggested calls from a fresh load each: (1) press r, drag from artboard (100,100) to (300,220); read X, Y, W, H, the layer list and the active tool; set W to 250 + Enter; press ArrowRight three times and Shift+ArrowDown once and read X and Y; press Control+d and read the new shape. (2) Draw an ellipse with Shift held and compare W and H. (3) Draw two rectangles at different x, Shift+click both, click Align left, read both X values; then marquee a region containing only one of them. (4) Layers: click +, draw an ellipse overlapping the rectangle, hide Layer 2 with its eye and try clicking where the ellipse was; show it again; lock Layer 1 and try selecting the rectangle; move Layer 1 up and see which shape is on top. (5) Resize with a corner handle and read W and H. (6) Undo: after draw, move and a fill change, press Control+z three times with screenshots, then Control+Shift+z. (7) Export SVG and read the dialog text. (8) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make the changes, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot or eval again.

rubric.criterion: The layout has the top bar with Undo, Redo and Export SVG, a tool rail with Select, Rectangle, Ellipse, Line and Text icons, an 800×500 white artboard on a gray workspace, the Inspector and Layers panels, and a status bar whose x and y match artboard coordinates.

Pressing R and dragging from artboard point (100,100) to (300,220) draws a #6366F1 rectangle that is selected with 8 handles, the Inspector reads X 100, Y 100, W 200, H 120 (within 1 px), the tool returns to Select and 'Rectangle 1' is listed under Layer 1.
Setting W to 250 and pressing Enter widens the rectangle; ArrowRight three times makes X 103 and Shift+ArrowDown makes Y 110, with the shape moving on the artboard to match.
Ctrl+D creates 'Rectangle 2' at X 113, Y 120 with the same size and selects it; Delete removes the selected shape.
Drawing an ellipse with Shift held produces a circle (W equals H), and a click without dragging draws nothing.
With two shapes selected by Shift+click, Align left gives both the same X equal to the leftmost original X; a marquee around only one shape selects only that shape.

Layers: + adds 'Layer 2' on top and makes it active so new shapes go there; hiding it removes its shapes from the artboard and makes them unselectable; locking Layer 1 prevents selecting its shapes; moving Layer 1 above Layer 2 draws its shapes on top.
Undo and redo step through changes one at a time: after drawing, moving and changing the fill, Ctrl+Z reverts the fill, then the move, then the drawing, and Ctrl+Shift+Z reapplies them.
Dragging a corner resize handle changes W and H in the Inspector to match the new size.
Export SVG shows markup with viewBox '0 0 800 500' and one g per visible layer, bottom layer first, each with data-name set to the layer name and containing its shapes.
After drawing shapes on two layers and reloading, the shapes, their positions and styles, and both layers with their names and order are restored.

It looks like a professional design tool: dark charcoal chrome, consistent 1.5 px line icons with a clear active tool state, a blue selection box with tidy handles, compact aligned inspector fields with tabular numbers.

title: Form builder with conditional logic, validation, pricing and JSON schema
prompt:
Build Formwright, a form builder with conditional logic, validation and a live JSON schema.

Views with hash routing, shown as header tabs: Build (#/build, the default), Preview (#/preview), JSON (#/json) and Responses (#/responses).

Build view: a palette of field types (Short text, Long text, Email, Number, Dropdown, Checkbox, Date), the form canvas listing the fields in order, and a settings panel for the selected field. Clicking a palette item appends that field and selects it. Settings: Label; Key (generated from the label in snake_case until edited by hand, must be unique, otherwise 'Key must be unique'); Required; type-specific rules (min and max for Number, earliest and latest date for Date, min length, max length and a regex pattern with a custom message for text, options one per line for Dropdown); and a 'Show when' rule made of another field, an operator (equals, does not equal, is checked, is not checked) and a value. Each canvas row has move up, move down, duplicate and delete buttons.

Seed the form 'Conference registration' with these fields in order:
1. full_name: Short text 'Full name', required, min length 2
2. email: Email 'Email', required
3. age: Number 'Age', required, min 18, max 120
4. ticket: Dropdown 'Ticket type', required, options Student, Standard, VIP
5. student_id: Short text 'Student ID', required, pattern ^S\d{6}$ with the message 'Use the format S123456', shown when ticket equals Student
6. workshop: Checkbox 'Add a workshop pass'
7. track: Dropdown 'Workshop track', required, options Design, Data, Security, shown when workshop is checked
8. arrival: Date 'Arrival date', required, from 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-06
9. notes: Long text 'Notes', max length 200, with a live counter like '0/200'

Preview view: the live form. Hidden fields are not shown, not validated and not submitted. Errors appear under a field when it loses focus and under every invalid field on submit, with exactly these messages: 'This field is required', 'Enter a valid email address', 'Must be at least 18', 'Must be at most 120', 'Must be at least 2 characters', 'Use the format S123456', 'Choose a date between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-06'. Submitting an invalid form shows 'Please fix N errors' above the form (N is the number of invalid visible fields) and focuses the first invalid field. A price line under the form updates live: Student $99, Standard $349, VIP $799, plus a workshop pass for $150 ($75 for students), shown like 'Total: $349'.

A valid submit shows 'Thanks, <full name>!' and the submitted JSON: keys in form order, only visible fields, numbers as numbers, the checkbox as true or false, plus a final 'total' key with the price as a number. Submissions are stored and listed in the Responses view as a table with one column per key and a 'N responses' count.

JSON view: the live schema as formatted JSON ({ title, fields: [{ key, type, label, required, rules, showWhen }] }) in an editable textarea with an Apply button; invalid JSON shows 'Invalid JSON' with the parser message and changes nothing.

The form and the responses persist in localStorage.

Visual direction: a tidy SaaS builder with white panels on a light gray background, one emerald accent, clear focus rings and red error text under fields. At 390px wide the Build view stacks palette, canvas and settings, and the preview form is one column.
interaction_hints: Navigate with the tabs or by setting location.hash. Fill fields with type and a selector, press Tab to blur; If clicking a select option does not work, use the select action or set it with eval (assign .value and dispatch input and change events). Date inputs accept values like 2026-11-03. Suggested calls from a fresh load each: (1) #/preview: count visible fields; click Submit with everything empty; read the summary, messages and document.activeElement. (2) Choose Student: Student ID appears and the total reads $99; check the workshop box: Workshop track appears, total $174; uncheck it. (3) Blur errors: full name A, email bob@, age 17 then 121, student id S12345, arrival 2026-11-08. (4) Valid submit: Ana Lima, ana@example.com, 29, Student, S204815, workshop checked, Data, 2026-11-03; read the JSON. Then switch ticket to VIP (with the workshop) and submit again: no student_id key, total 949; open #/responses. (5) Build: click Number in the palette, set the label to Group size (check the key becomes group_size), min 1, max 10, Show when ticket equals VIP; check the preview for Standard and for VIP. Set a key to email to see the uniqueness error; move a field up and check the preview order. (6) #/json: change the label Age to Your age and Apply; then apply broken JSON. (7) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make the changes, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot or eval again. Check mobile.png.

rubric.criterion: The header has Build, Preview, JSON and Responses tabs that change the hash (#/build, #/preview, #/json, #/responses); the Build view shows the palette, the canvas with the nine seeded fields in order and a settings panel for the selected field.
The preview first shows 7 fields (Student ID and Workshop track hidden); choosing Student shows Student ID, checking the workshop box shows Workshop track, and unchecking hides it again.
Submitting the empty preview shows 'Please fix 5 errors', 'This field is required' under Full name, Email, Age, Ticket type and Arrival date, and moves focus to Full name.

Blur validation shows exactly: 'Must be at least 2 characters' for A, 'Enter a valid email address' for bob@, 'Must be at least 18' for 17, 'Must be at most 120' for 121, 'Use the format S123456' for S12345 and 'Choose a date between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-06' for 2026-11-08.

title: Project planner with Gantt chart, working-day scheduling and critical path
prompt:
Build Critpath, a project planner with a task table, a Gantt chart, dependencies and critical-path analysis.

Project 'Atlas web launch' starts on Monday 2 November 2026. Working days are Monday to Friday, and 26 and 27 November 2026 are holidays. Durations are in working days and every dependency is finish-to-start: a task starts on the first working day after all its predecessors finish, or on the project start if it has none. A task's finish is its last working day (a 3-day task starting Mon 2 Nov finishes Wed 4 Nov).

Seed these tasks (ID, name, duration, depends on):
T1 Kickoff and requirements, 3, none
T2 UX research, 5, T1
T3 Architecture design, 4, T1
T4 UI design, 6, T2
T5 Backend API, 10, T3
T6 Database schema, 3, T3
T7 Frontend build, 8, T4 and T6
T8 Integration, 4, T5 and T7
T9 QA and bug bash, 5, T8
T10 Docs and training, 3, T7
T11 Launch, 1, T9 and T10

Task table (left): ID, Name, Duration, Depends on, Start, Finish and Slack (working days the task can slip without moving the project finish). Name, Duration and Depends on (comma-separated IDs) are editable inline; Enter commits and Escape cancels. Durations must be whole numbers from 1 to 60. Invalid input is rejected with an inline message and the old value restored: 'Unknown task T99' for a missing ID, and 'Circular dependency: ' followed by the loop for a cycle (like 'T2 → T4 → T2'). 'Add task' appends the next ID with a 1-day duration and no dependencies; deleting a task also removes it from other tasks' dependencies. Dates show like 'Wed 4 Nov'.

Gantt chart (right): one row per task aligned with the table, a date header with day numbers grouped under month names, weekend and holiday columns shaded, a bar from each task's start to its finish, dependency arrows from each predecessor's bar end to its successor's bar start, and a thin line after each non-critical bar showing its slack. Critical tasks (zero slack) are red and the others use the accent color. Hovering a bar shows a tooltip with its dates and slack. A Day / Week zoom switch changes the column width.

Summary strip: 'Finish: ' with the project finish date written like 'Mon 1 Feb 2027', 'Duration: N working days', and 'Critical path: ' with the critical task IDs joined by arrows.

Everything recalculates immediately after any edit. Undo and redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) cover edits, adds and deletes. The plan persists in localStorage.

Visual direction: a professional planning tool: white background, fine gray gridlines, compact 13 px table text with tabular numbers, one blue accent for bars, red for the critical path and a sticky date header.
interaction_hints: Edit a cell by clicking or double-clicking it (whichever the app uses), typing and pressing Enter; read the table and the summary with eval (innerText) and screenshots. Suggested calls from a fresh load each: (1) read the table, summary and which bars are red; check that the Nov 26-27 and weekend columns are shaded and that T7's bar spans them. (2) Set T6 duration to 9; read the summary, T2 and T4 slack and T7 dates. (3) Set T5 duration to 14; read T3 and T5 slack and the finish. (4) Set T3's dependencies to T1, T7 (a cycle), then set T8's dependencies to T5, T99; check the messages and that the old values stay. (5) Add task: read the new T12 row; delete T10 and read T11's dependencies and the finish. (6) After an edit press Control+z and Control+y. (7) Hover a bar for the tooltip; switch Day/Week zoom. (8) localStorage starts empty in every new interact call, so test persistence inside ONE call: make the changes, then eval 'setTimeout(() => location.reload(), 50)', wait 1500 ms and screenshot or eval again.

rubric.criterion: The table lists T1 to T11 with ID, Name, Duration, Depends on, Start, Finish and Slack, next to a Gantt chart with month and day headers where weekends and the 26-27 November holidays are shaded.
Computed dates: T1 Mon 2 Nov to Wed 4 Nov, T3 Thu 5 Nov to Tue 10 Nov, T5 Wed 11 Nov to Tue 24 Nov, T7 Fri 20 Nov to Thu 3 Dec (skipping the holidays), T9 Thu 10 Dec to Wed 16 Dec and T11 Thu 17 Dec.

The summary reads Finish Thu 17 Dec 2026, Duration 32 working days and Critical path T1 → T2 → T4 → T7 → T8 → T9 → T11; exactly those bars are red, and the slack column shows T3 4, T5 5, T6 4 and T10 6.
Changing T6's duration to 9 gives Finish Mon 21 Dec 2026, 34 working days, Critical path T1 → T3 → T6 → T7 → T8 → T9 → T11, slack 2 for T2 and T4, and T7 from Tue 24 Nov to Mon 7 Dec.
Changing T5's duration to 14 keeps Finish Thu 17 Dec 2026 and sets the slack of T5 and T3 to 1.

Add task creates T12 with duration 1 starting Mon 2 Nov with slack 31; deleting T10 removes it from T11's dependencies and the finish stays Thu 17 Dec 2026.
